$doc: What the renderer reports of a frame (pxl-render gpu/renderer.rs): the GPU spans it is timed in,
in the order the renderer encodes them, and the kind of frame it made; the profiler records and reports
$GPU_SPAN_NAMES: `world` is the world's pass as it lays the opaque world, and `world_rest` the pass that goes on after the occlusion is found between them (`ao`), drawing over it the occlusion's map, the sky and what the kernel animates; where the occlusion is not found again the one pass draws it all, timed as `world`, and `world_rest` runs none. A span is `per_px` where a pass it times runs threads over the world's drawn pixels, its fragments or a thread a pixel or a square of them, so its cost goes with the drawn resolution: the world's passes, its occlusion, its gathering and the depth's bound (`resolve`), the boxes' raster into the visibility buffer (`sraster`), the pixels' cast and their misses' walk, and the marks drawn over the world's depth with their propagation over its squares (`mark`); the drawn resolution's scale is judged on these alone (pxl-render gpu/renderer.rs `px_ms`, pxl-kernel domain/view/frame/resolution.rs). Not `per_px`: the camera grid's beam rays, cells, samples and their boxes' faces, on its own angular lattice (`beam`, `cell`, `sample`, `face`); the observed pyramid's forgetting, over its entries (`cast`); and the canvas's passes, at the display's pixels (`finish`, `marker`, `debug`).
$LIGHT_MOVED: Why the light's map cast, a bit each, bit k the k-th (pxl-render gpu/ray/cast.rs `light_moved`): what it reads moved, the light's frame, the eye's zooms its bands are held to, the world under it or the shadows' setting (`content`); the box slid (`slide`); which tiles the receivers read, the eye's place and look, the actors' places or decor compacted again (`receivers`); or the footprints owed the first frame the eye stands in after it moved (`footprint`).
$FRAME_KINDS: What the renderer made of a frame turn, where it decides it (pxl-render gpu/renderer.rs `render_frame`, `FrameKind`): `none` before it was asked; `unready` with no device or surface, or while the renderer is made before its first frame (`Pipelines::share`); `held` where the surfaces would block (not admitted); `dropped` where the frame did not fit the GPU stream; `plain` drawn with nothing cast; `standing` drawn on the standing ray lane; `cast` drawn with a cast; `stood` where nothing the frame reads changed, so nothing is drawn or submitted and the canvases keep what they show; `px` drawn with the pixels cast again over samples that stood, where only the eye's jitter moved (pxl-spec-core `eye::JITTER`); `gated` drawn through the gate where only what the kernel bounds moved: the claimed screen tiles alone drawn again, the rest standing (pxl-render gpu/renderer.rs `GATE_NUMBERS`, screen_tiles.wgsl).
